changelog.title: What changed in {league}
changelog.how: Every change has a short summary. Select Impact to see what it means for your character, your farming and your gear.
changelog.section.big.desc: Changes that alter how you play, farm or gear. Read these first.
changelog.section.small.desc: Number tweaks and adjustments. Skim for your build and your favourite content.
changelog.section.new.desc: Things that did not exist before this patch.
changelog.empty: Nothing in this section for the selected topic.
impact.confidence.confirmed: Follows directly from the official patch notes.
impact.confidence.prediction: Our reading of the notes and early community reports. It may change as the league develops.
builds.title: Builds for {league}
builds.lede: Each build is explained from the core idea down to the details. Read the top of an article to decide, and open the expandable parts when you need to know why.
builds.group.starter.desc: Builds that work on a fresh character with no currency, and carry you into maps.
builds.group.endgame.desc: High-budget builds to move to once you have currency.
builds.none: Endgame builds will be added once the first week of the league shows what works.
builds.budget.title: What the budget labels mean
builds.budget.note: There is no live price feed. These are rough ranges, and prices in the first week of a league move fast.
build.budget.starter.desc: Self-found gear and a few Chaos Orbs.
build.pieces.note: The build does not function without the pieces marked Must. Everything else is a strong recommendation.
build.progression.note: Five stages from level 1 to the endgame. Each says what you use, what changes, and when to move on. Open the expandable parts for detail.
build.sources.note: We read these and cross-checked them against each other and the official notes. Where they disagree, the article says so.
leveling.title: Leveling: level 1 to the end of Act 10
leveling.campaign: The whole campaign at a glance
leveling.campaign.note: Ten acts in order. Each card shows the act boss, the passive points you can earn, and the events that fall in that act: Labyrinths, resistance penalties and unlocks.
leveling.howToRead.note: Each act page draws the zones as a flow chart in travel order. Side trips branch off to the right. Every zone carries one of four labels. Select a zone to see the quest, the reward and how to handle it.
leveling.principles: Nine habits for a smooth campaign
leveling.route.note: Zones in travel order. {must} required stops, {worth} side trips worth taking, {skip} you can skip. Select a zone for details.
leveling.labs.full: The full Labyrinth guide: trials, rules and traps
donate.title: Thanks for reading
donate.body: I do not run this site to make money. But if you would like to buy me a coffee, or a hotpot, I would be very happy.
donate.close: No thanks, back to the guide
donate.footer: This guide is free and always will be.
leveling.map.note: Every zone in travel order, with side areas hanging off the zone they branch from, and a number on each zone where a quest happens. Select anything to open it. Zone layouts are built fresh each time you enter one, so what a map can honestly show is this: what connects to what, and where the quests are.

build.early.title: Early game: levelling and your first maps
build.early.note: From level 1 to white and yellow maps. Each stage says what you use, what changes, and when to move on.
build.endgame.title: Endgame: red maps and beyond
build.endgame.note: Where the build becomes what it is. The stages first, then how its power grows, what to buy in which order, how to play it, and what to do when it goes wrong.
build.upgrades: What to buy next, in order
build.upgrades.note: Ordered by what each step buys for its price. The reason beside each one is why it sits where it does.
build.deaths.note: The usual ways it goes wrong, the reason behind each, and the fix.
build.troubleshooting.note: Find the symptom, read the cause.
updates.title: What has changed since launch
updates.lede: Every hotfix, patch and developer post since {league} went live, newest first, rewritten in plain language with what it means for your character.
updates.how: Each one carries one of two labels. In the game means you are already playing with it. Not live yet means the developers have announced it: the numbers in it are a plan until a patch ships them.
updates.empty: Nothing to show for that choice.
updates.none: No updates since launch yet. This page fills in as Grinding Gear Games ships them.
updates.since.build: Since launch: updates that touch this build
updates.since.build.note: Hotfixes and developer posts published after the league started. The article above was written before them; read these alongside it.
craft.title: Item Crafting Guide
craft.lede: How to craft every kind of item with the tools that are in the game every league: currency, the crafting bench, beasts, Essences, Fossils and the rest.
craft.none: The crafting guide is being written.
craft.start.anatomy.text: Rarity, prefixes and suffixes, item level, tiers and weights. Everything else rests on these.
craft.start.toolbox.text: Every permanent crafting tool, from the first Orb of Transmutation to meta-crafting, in the order you will meet them.
craft.start.strands.text: What Memory Strands on an item do to every currency you use on it.
craft.pick: Pick what you want to craft
craft.pick.note: Each category is its own guide: what the bases are, how to read the modifiers, how to plan a craft from nothing, and worked examples from a first craft to the hardest ones.
craft.section.special: Special modifiers and where they come from
craft.basics.all.note: Straight from the game data. Level is the level needed to equip the base, which is also the lowest area level it drops at. Open a group to see its bases.
craft.tools.note: Only tools that are in the game every league. Each one links to its full explanation.
craft.strands.more: The full explanation of Memory Strands
craft.special.note: These do not come from plain rolling. Each needs a particular source.
craft.sources.note: The numbers come from the game data export. The method comes from the sources below, checked against each other.
craft.pool.legend: The bar is how likely one random modifier on this side is from that family. Open a row for every tier.
craft.examples.lede: Worked crafts for {name}, from the first one you should try to the hardest. Each says what to do, why, and what the item looks like after every step.
craft.examples.none: Examples for this category are being written.
craft.example.base: The base and the item level
craft.example.needs: What you need before you start
craft.mods.lede: Every modifier {name} can have: what rolls naturally, what the bench adds, and what only comes from Essences, influence, veiled modifiers or Fossils.
craft.mods.how: Pick the kind of base to see its pool. The bar and the percentage show how likely a single random modifier on that side is to come from that family, when the item level allows every tier.
craft.mods.bench.note: What the bench can add, with the cost of each rank. A bench modifier takes a prefix or suffix slot like any other.
craft.mods.essence.note: Using an Essence rerolls the item as a Rare with this modifier guaranteed.
craft.mods.veiled.note: What a veiled modifier can turn into when it is unveiled.
craft.mods.influence.note: Extra modifiers an influenced base can roll, on top of the normal pool. The item-level range runs from the lowest tier to the highest.
craft.mods.delve.note: These roll only when the item is crafted with the right Fossil.
craft.mods.implicit.note: Eldritch implicits come from Ichors and Embers; a Vaal Orb can replace the implicit with one of the corruption implicits. The best tier of each is shown.
craft.mods.source: Modifier and base data: the game data export, via
craft.how.title: How crafting works
craft.how.lede: The ideas and the tools every category guide relies on. Read this once and the rest of the section will make sense.
craft.toolbox.note: Ordered from the tools you use on day one to the ones that only make sense on an expensive item. The pips show how advanced each one is.
home.card.crafting: How to craft every kind of item, from the base and its modifiers to worked examples, easy to hard.
craft.mods.cluster.note: A cluster jewel's enchantment is the small passive it adds. It is fixed on the item, and it decides which notables can roll. Open an enchantment to see its notables, the item level each needs, and how likely each is among the notables of that enchantment.
